title: fr and intrinsic sizing
learningObjectives: Explain fr and intrinsic sizing and choose suitable CSS values for a responsive layout.

understand.concept: The fr unit represents a fraction of the available space in a CSS Grid container after relevant fixed and intrinsic contributions are considered. Intrinsic sizing keywords such as min-content, max-content, and auto describe content-based sizing behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: Grid tracks do not always divide space equally when minimum sizes and long content affect the layout. Understanding intrinsic sizing helps prevent overflow and unexpected track widths.
understand.analogy: The fr unit divides remaining layout space into shares, while intrinsic sizes ask how much room the content itself needs.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual sizing follows CSS value resolution and layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The middle track receives twice the fractional share of each outer track, subject to grid sizing rules.

examples.explanation: The middle track receives twice the fractional share of each outer track, subject to grid sizing rules.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the relevant CSS unit or math function.

practise.guidedTask: Change the tracks to min-content 1fr max-content. Observe what happens with a long unbroken word.
practise.independentTask: Create a small responsive component using the concept. Test narrow and wide viewports, long text, and browser zoom.
hints: Inspect computed values in developer tools.
Change one unit at a time.
Avoid fixed dimensions that unnecessarily clip content.
